observations.statement: The core declares a prompt-taking SQL-injection checker returning Result<(), GuardError>, with only comments naming common patterns in its body.
Repeated destructive-command attempts are described as an enhancement that may increase strictness or block an agent, and the shown state holds violation timestamps, a maximum, and a window length.

GUI controls that reduce FileSafe enforcement are globally required to use authenticated operator authorization with scoped duration and reason plus an audit receipt; the destructive override additionally names realm, identity, scope, expiry, audit event, and receipt.
Assistant chat offers one-run approval and persistent approval, while command-blocklist evaluation gives approved commands precedence and permits exact or normalized matching.
Prompt Pipeline owns context compilation, while FileSafe is limited to checks over the fully compiled prompt and attachments after assembly and before provider dispatch.

The BaseRunner sketch performs circuit-breaker, quota, and rate-limit checks before FileSafe, checks the reconstructed command and extracted paths, then reaches permission audit and spawn continuation.
The integration rules require Arc sharing, existing logging, canonical-event-stream violation records, fail-closed canonicalization, and prohibition of unresolved-path fallback.
Verification-gate classification is transported through PUPPET_MASTER_OPERATION_TYPE in ExecutionRequest.env_vars and set by the orchestrator.
The path extractor is described as finding paths that might be written from prompt text, context files, extra arguments, and common prompt patterns, then sorting and deduplicating them.
Write-scope authorization is transported through PUPPET_MASTER_ALLOWED_FILES rather than a dedicated ExecutionRequest field, and serialization failure is converted to a default string.
The core presents both exact-value and prefix-value interview classifiers, and separately proposes interview configuration whose sensitive-read default is true and strict-file-guard default is false.
Worktree-aware write scope is required to resolve project-relative paths against the request working directory and compare only against the request-derived allowlist.

Cleanup coordination is required not to be prevented by write-scope violations, and guard, gate, or wiring outcomes become enforceable schema/evidence promises only when machine-readable contracts can represent them.
The GUI authority is assigned to FinalGUISpec, and FileSafe is placed as a collapsible FileSafe Guards card under Settings > Advanced rather than as a separate tab.

The Assistant Chat contract specifies a persistent YOLO warning, a blocked-command card, one-time and persistent approval actions, a 60-second timeout, event logging, and prefixed red terminal output.

The following context, not used to substantiate a core finding, requires GUI FileSafe configuration and approved commands to be wired through orchestrator configuration into BaseRunner initialization.
The following context, not used to substantiate a core finding, repeats that verification gates run after iterations and may need destructive commands.

candidate_findings.title: SQL-injection guard has no executable behavior contract
candidate_findings.statement: The checker is only a signature plus comments; the core does not define the pattern grammar, normalization and encoding rules, attachment coverage, error variant, allow/block result, or platform-runner call that realizes this safety check.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can implement incompatible detection, omit material inputs, or leave the declared check inert while still matching the shown skeleton.

candidate_findings.title: Repeated-violation rate limiting lacks a state machine
candidate_findings.statement: The enhancement and data fields do not define the agent identity key, threshold boundary, fixed versus sliding window, timestamp pruning, strictness change, block duration, reset or unblock transition, concurrency behavior, persistence, emitted error, or integration call.
candidate_findings.impact: Repeated destructive attempts can receive materially different enforcement across implementations, including no effective escalation.

candidate_findings.title: Chat approval actions are not bound to the mandatory authorization grant
candidate_findings.statement: The global contract requires authenticated, scoped, expiring, reasoned, receipted enforcement reductions, but the one-click approval and add-to-list flows do not specify how the selected blocked command is bound to realm, operator identity, reason, scope, expiry, audit event, and receipt.
candidate_findings.impact: An implementation may treat a UI click or persistent-list mutation as sufficient authority and bypass the stated operator-control boundary.

candidate_findings.title: Approved-command normalized matching is undefined
candidate_findings.statement: The command whitelist may use exact or normalized matching, with whitespace stripping only as an example, but no canonical algorithm defines whitespace, quoting, escaping, environment assignments, path forms, case, or argument-boundary treatment.
candidate_findings.impact: Over-broad normalization can approve destructive variants, while under-broad normalization can fail approved commands; behavior is consequentially left to builders.

candidate_findings.title: FileSafe check ordering is internally inconsistent
candidate_findings.statement: The integration comment says to add guards before existing checks, while the numbered sketch places existing circuit-breaker, quota, and rate-limit checks before FileSafe and permission audit after it.
candidate_findings.impact: Different implementations can place safety checks at different lifecycle points, changing which resources, side effects, and audit events occur before a command is rejected.

candidate_findings.title: Command matching uses an unspecified reconstructed representation
candidate_findings.statement: The command guard evaluates a string made by concatenating self.command with args joined by one space, but the core does not define escaping or preservation of original argument boundaries and then permits exact or normalized approved-list matching against that representation.
candidate_findings.impact: The guarded or approved text can diverge from the command's actual argument structure, producing false blocks or unsafe approvals.

candidate_findings.title: Verification-gate tag bypasses destructive-command enforcement without the required grant
candidate_findings.statement: A blocklist error is converted to a warning and execution continues whenever the request's operation type equals verification_gate, while the core's enforcement-reduction rule requires authenticated operator authority, reason, scope, expiry, event, and receipt; no such binding is shown for the tag.
candidate_findings.impact: Any request accepted as a verification gate receives an automatic destructive-command bypass outside the specified authorization boundary.

candidate_findings.title: Verification-gate sensitive-file allowance is promised but not wired
candidate_findings.statement: The gate detector's rationale says security audits may need to read sensitive files, but the BaseRunner path loop calls the security filter unconditionally and only the command-blocklist error has a verification-gate branch.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders cannot tell whether gate-sensitive reads must remain blocked or be relaxed, and the shown behavior cannot satisfy the stated gate rationale.

candidate_findings.title: Path enforcement depends on heuristic request-text discovery
candidate_findings.statement: The same extracted-path loop drives write-scope and sensitive-file checks, while the extractor promises only potential paths found through prompt phrases, context files, extra arguments, and common patterns; it defines no complete mapping from an executed operation to every accessed or written path.
candidate_findings.impact: A file path absent from the heuristic request representation has no specified route through either guard, leaving safety coverage incomplete and implementation-dependent.

candidate_findings.title: Context files are ambiguously treated as write targets
candidate_findings.statement: The extractor says context files are already allowed and need a security-filter check, yet it adds them to the same vector that BaseRunner sends through file_guard.check_file_write before the security filter.
candidate_findings.impact: Read-only context can be falsely blocked as an unauthorized write, or builders may special-case it inconsistently and accidentally skip the security check.

candidate_findings.title: Nonexistent write-target resolution is unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The extractor explicitly covers create and write instructions, but every canonicalize failure is mapped to SymlinkResolution and the core defines no parent-resolution or other rule for a destination that cannot yet be canonicalized.
candidate_findings.impact: Allowed creation can fail closed indistinguishably from a path-safety violation, or builders may invent unsafe fallback behavior despite the fallback prohibition.

candidate_findings.title: Allowed-files environment transport lacks parse and failure semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The plan chooses a JSON-bearing environment variable and silently substitutes a default string on serialization failure, but does not define the variable schema, malformed-input result, diagnostic event, size limits, duplicate handling, path normalization, or how load_allowed_files_from_request distinguishes missing, empty, and invalid values.
candidate_findings.impact: Equivalent requests can block differently, and serialization or parsing failures can become opaque operational failures rather than attributable guard evidence.

candidate_findings.title: Interview operation detection has incompatible definitions
candidate_findings.statement: One BaseRunner definition recognizes only the exact value interview, while a later definition with the same function name recognizes values beginning interview_.
candidate_findings.impact: The document cannot be implemented literally as one coherent classifier, and interview guard relaxation depends on which incompatible rule a builder selects.

candidate_findings.title: Interview defaults contradict scoped enforcement-reduction authority
candidate_findings.statement: The interview section says the security filter should be more permissive and defaults allow_sensitive_file_read to true, while the earlier core requires every enforcement reduction to be authenticated, scoped in duration and reason, audited, and receipted and says a missing security baseline still blocks.
candidate_findings.impact: Sensitive-file access may become broadly enabled by default instead of through an explicit, expiring operator grant.

candidate_findings.title: Worktree allowlist authorization check is omitted
candidate_findings.statement: The FileGuard sketch resolves and canonicalizes the path, then contains only a comment to check against normalized allowed files and an ellipsis; it defines no membership algorithm, directory or glob semantics, case behavior, symlink-root containment, missing-entry result, or returned success and error paths.
candidate_findings.impact: The central write-scope authorization decision is not buildable from this window and can be implemented with materially different escape boundaries.

candidate_findings.title: Cleanup exception has no bounded authority contract
candidate_findings.statement: Write-scope violations must not prevent worktree cleanup and cleanup must not delete allowed files, but the core does not define the cleanup actor, authorized operations and roots, ordering after a violation, partial-failure behavior, retry or idempotency, or required audit evidence.
candidate_findings.impact: Cleanup can either remain blocked and leak worktrees or gain an overly broad guard bypass that deletes data outside its intended scope.

candidate_findings.title: Persistent toggle state is not separated from expiring override state
candidate_findings.statement: The core allows independent GUI controls and persists FileSafe changes, while any enforcement reduction must have scoped duration, reason, expiry, event, and receipt; no state model distinguishes configured intent, pending request, active grant, effective enforcement, expiry, revocation, and restored state.
candidate_findings.impact: A builder may persist disabled enforcement beyond an authorized duration or restore an incorrect state after expiry or restart.

candidate_findings.title: Blocked-command approval lacks concurrency and terminal-state semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The inline card specifies two actions and a 60-second auto-dismiss, but no command or request correlation identifier, cancellation rule, click-at-timeout ordering, duplicate-click idempotency, concurrent-card behavior, retry behavior, or post-approval execution receipt.
candidate_findings.impact: A late or repeated action can run the wrong command, run a command twice, or disagree with the displayed timed-out state.

candidate_findings.title: Timed approval UI lacks accessibility behavior
candidate_findings.statement: The blocked-command UI specifies an orange border, monospace text, action labels, and automatic dismissal after 60 seconds, but no keyboard order, focus transfer or restoration, assistive-technology announcement, accessible countdown, pause or extension mechanism, or reduced-motion behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Keyboard and assistive-technology users may miss the block reason or lose the opportunity to act before automatic dismissal.

candidate_findings.title: Approved-command persistence authority is unresolved
candidate_findings.statement: The list may live in puppet-master.yaml or a dedicated file, while the GUI config also carries approved_commands and saves Advanced-tab changes; the core does not choose the authoritative store or define migration, synchronization, atomic update, permission, corruption, or concurrent-edit behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: The UI and runtime can observe different whitelists, and a partial or weakly protected update can alter command authority unpredictably.

candidate_findings.title: Machine-readable acceptance oracle is only gestured at
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires evidence-schema or wiring-evidence representation before guard, gate, or wiring promises are enforceable, but defines no required fields, producer, consumer, identifiers, pass/fail rule, receipt correlation, or acceptance fixtures in this window.
candidate_findings.impact: A build can emit prose or structurally divergent evidence without an objective oracle for FileSafe wiring and behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Event-log contract lacks security and lifecycle semantics
candidate_findings.statement: Violations must reach the canonical event stream and blocked commands are exposed through an event-log viewer or link, but the core does not define event schema, command redaction, access control, retention, ordering, pagination, receipt correlation, or failure behavior when logging is unavailable.
candidate_findings.impact: Audit evidence can be incomplete or leak sensitive command content, and operator receipts cannot be reliably correlated to blocked or approved executions.

candidate_findings.title: Path-extraction comment and condition disagree
candidate_findings.statement: The extractor comment says to skip URLs and absolute paths that are clearly not file operations, but the shown condition filters only http and https prefixes and specifies no absolute-path test.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementers following prose versus code will produce different path sets and therefore different write-scope and sensitive-file enforcement.

candidate_findings.title: Config-save transaction boundary remains an explicit alternative
candidate_findings.statement: FileSafe changes may use Save Changes per tab or a global save, with no chosen commit boundary, validation order, rollback, partial-save, or restart-on-failure contract.
candidate_findings.impact: Guard state and approved-command mutations can become partially persisted or take effect at different times across implementations.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Write scope explicitly fails closed when the allowlist is missing or empty, and the security filter explicitly fails closed when its baseline is missing.
The destructive-override authorization inputs are explicit: auth realm, operator identity, reason, scope, expiry, audit event, and receipt.
Canonical ownership and lifecycle placement for context compilation versus FileSafe prompt checks are explicit.
Path-resolution failure is explicitly fail-closed, and fallback to the unresolved original path is explicitly prohibited.
The canonical event stream is explicitly authoritative for guard violations, with filesafe-events.jsonl only a derived mirror.
The transport choice for request-scoped allowed files is explicit: ExecutionRequest.env_vars[PUPPET_MASTER_ALLOWED_FILES], not a new allowed_files field.
Worktree-relative paths are explicitly resolved from the request working directory rather than an unspecified process directory.
Live GUI placement is explicit and overrides the retired separate-tab lineage: Settings > Advanced contains a collapsible FileSafe Guards card.
The blocked-command UI explicitly defines action labels, a 60-second skipped-command outcome, blocked-event logging, and a textual terminal prefix in addition to red color.
The core explicitly requires machine-readable representation before schema and evidence promises are treated as enforceable.
Approved commands explicitly take precedence over the command blocklist for matching commands.

FileSafe settings must be **configurable in the GUI** and centrally inspectable. All FileSafe controls live in one place (dedicated FileSafe tab or clearly grouped section). Any control that reduces enforcement must route through explicit authenticated operator authorization, scoped duration/reason, and audit receipt.
- **Write scope** -- "Restrict writes to plan" (enforced/request scoped override). Missing or empty allowlist still blocks.
- **Security filter** -- "Block sensitive files" (enforced/request scoped override). Missing baseline still blocks.

- **Override:** "Request destructive override" (with prominent warning) for Command blocklist. It never succeeds from UI state alone; it requires auth realm, operator identity, reason, scope, expiry, audit event, and receipt.

- When a command is blocked by the Command blocklist in Assistant chat, the user can **approve this run** and optionally **add to approved list**. Approved commands are stored in settings and are then allowed by the command blocklist (whitelist overrides blocklist for matching commands).

- In Config (FileSafe section), the user can **view** the list of approved commands, **remove** entries, and (optionally) **add** entries manually. List is persisted (e.g. in `puppet-master.yaml` under `filesafe.approvedCommands` or a dedicated file).

- Implementation: Command blocklist checks the approved list before blocking; exact match or normalized match (e.g. strip extra whitespace) counts as approved. UX: In chat, show "Blocked: <command>" with actions "Approve once" and "Approve and add to list"; in settings, show scrollable list with remove button per row.

**Current Architecture:**
- Interview orchestrator spawns agents for research, validation, document generation
- Uses same `BaseRunner` infrastructure
- No special FileSafe considerations currently

**Integration Points:**

1. **Interview-Specific Guards:**
   - Research operations may need to read sensitive files (e.g., `.env` for understanding config)
   - Security filter should be more permissive during interview phases
   - Add interview phase detection:

- Worktrees are created per subtask for parallel execution
- `BaseRunner` receives `working_directory` which may be a worktree path
- Guards must operate in the correct working directory context

1. **Worktree-aware write scope:**
   - File paths in plans are relative to project root
   - Guards must resolve paths relative to `working_directory` (which may be a worktree)
   - Write-scope checks must account for worktree structure

- Write-scope violations should not prevent worktree cleanup
   - MiscPlan cleanup should respect write-scope allowed files (don't delete allowed files)
   - Coordinate with `cleanup_after_execution` in runner contract
   - Structured gate details use `Plans/evidence.schema.json` (`/evidence.schema.json`) gate-specific blocks or a dedicated `wiring-evidence` block so machine-readable wiring results do not remain prose-only.
   - FileSafe treats `/schema` and `/evidence` promises as enforceable only when the machine-readable contract can represent the same guard, gate, or wiring outcome.
**Authority:** **Plans/FinalGUISpec.md §7.4 (Advanced tab)** and **§7.16 (Assistant Chat)** are the canonical GUI spec. This section aligns FileSafe.md with that spec.

- Config view had 8 tabs: Tiers, Branching, Verification, Memory, Budgets, Advanced, Interview, YAML. This is a retired compatibility note only; live Settings placement follows FinalGUISpec §7.4.4 and the required Advanced-card placement below.

- FileSafe is **not** a separate tab. It lives under **Settings > Advanced** as a **collapsible card** titled **"FileSafe Guards"**.
- Same Advanced tab contains MCP Configuration, Tool permissions, and Other (experimental, cleanup, etc.). FileSafe is one collapsible card among these.

- **Three independent enforcement controls** (product labels; internal keys remain `bash_guard` / `file_guard` / `security_filter`):
  - **"Block destructive commands"** -- Command blocklist state and scoped override request.
  - **"Restrict writes to plan"** -- Write scope state and scoped override request; empty/missing allowlist remains blocked.
  - **"Block sensitive files"** -- Security filter state and scoped override request; missing baseline remains blocked.
- **Override:** "Request destructive override" control with **prominent warning styling** (e.g. danger/warning variant per widget catalog).
- **Approved commands:** Scrollable list; per-row **Remove** button; optional **"Add command manually"**; persisted in `filesafe.approvedCommands` (e.g. `puppet-master.yaml`).
**Config struct (unchanged):** `GuiConfig.filesafe: FileSafeConfig` with `BashGuardConfig`, `FileGuardConfig`, `SecurityFilterConfig`, `approved_commands: Vec<String>` as in §2.4 and §5.2.

- **YOLO + FileSafe:** When YOLO is enabled and FileSafe guards are active, show a **persistent warning chip** in the input toolbar: **"[!] YOLO active -- FileSafe guards still apply."**
- **In-chat approval when blocked:** When FileSafe blocks a command during YOLO (or when a blocked command is shown in chat), display an **inline card** in the chat stream:
  - **Style:** Orange left border; command text in monospace; guard name that triggered (e.g. "Command blocklist").
  - **Actions:** **"Approve once"** (runs the command this time only) and **"Approve & add to list"** (adds to `filesafe.approvedCommands` in Settings > Advanced).
  - **Timeout:** Card auto-dismisses after **60 seconds** with message "Timed out -- command skipped."
  - **Logging:** Blocked commands are logged to the FileSafe event log; accessible from Settings > Advanced (event log viewer or link).
- **Terminal (FinalGUISpec §7.16):** When a command is blocked by FileSafe, terminal output uses **RED** with prefix **"[BLOCKED] Blocked by FileSafe"**.
- **FileSafe status (optional):** Compact card showing guard count (e.g. "FileSafe: 3/3 guards active") with link to **Settings > Advanced > FileSafe**.
- Config save: FileSafe changes persist with the rest of Advanced tab (Save Changes per tab or global).

- FileSafe config must be wired to `PuppetMasterConfig` (orchestrator config).
- Follow Option B pattern from `Plans/WorktreeGitImprovement.md` §5.2 (Chosen approach: Option B -- Build run config from GUI): build run config from GUI config at orchestrator start.
- Ensure FileSafe settings (and `approved_commands`) are available to `BaseRunner` initialization so the command blocklist whitelist is applied at runtime.

- Verification gates run AFTER iteration completion
- Gates check evidence, run tests, verify acceptance criteria
- Gate operations may legitimately need destructive commands (e.g., test database resets)
